s: Cross-encoder model that re-scores initial retrieval results by computing precise query-document relevance scores.
w: After initial retrieval (vector search or BM25), the reranker takes each candidate document along with the query and computes a fine-grained relevance score using a cross-encoder model. Unlike bi-encoder embeddings, cross-encoders see both query and document simultaneously for deeper understanding. Top-K candidates become top-N reranked results. This adds latency (~10-50ms per document) but significantly improves precision.
use: RAG pipelines where initial vector retrieval precision is insufficient
Search result quality improvement for user-facing search
Hybrid search merging: rerank combined BM25 + vector results for unified ranking
Recommendation refinement: narrow broad similarity results to truly relevant items
avoid: Initial retrieval stage (too slow for full-corpus scoring; use embeddings for first-pass)
High-volume real-time paths where latency is critical without batching
Small result sets (<5 candidates) where overhead exceeds marginal quality gain

props.top_k: Number of candidates to rerank from initial retrieval

pat.d: Fast first-pass (vector/BM25) then precise second-pass (cross-encoder reranker).

pits: Latency budget exceeded if too many candidates passed to reranker - tune top_k carefully
Model mismatch between embedding model and reranker - ensure they share semantic understanding
tips: Bi-encoder vs cross-encoder distinction is the key concept: fast approximate vs slow precise
Reranker improves recall@K significantly even when K is small (5-20 candidates)
